conviction.explanation: Medium evidence confidence. The bear carries the current-price objection because comparable-demand quality does not demonstrate owner-cash value at 44.49x vendor earnings. Annual growth survives tariff normalisation, so a business-decline sell thesis is unsupported. Normalised membership economics and cash valuation are required for a stronger purchase ruling. Conviction describes the current evidence, not a calibrated win rate; outcome memory has no observations.

executive_summary:
Costco grew FY26 sales 10.1%, adjusted annual comparable sales 6.6% and annual net income. This supports operating quality, but its vendor trailing multiple of 44.49x requires sustained earnings duration and Q4 EPS includes a $0.15 tariff-refund benefit; quality has not independently established cheapness. Maintain observation; the evidence does not yet establish a directional new-position advantage.

Price has only narrowly reclaimed SMA-50 and remains below SMA-200 despite a strengthening positive MACD histogram. Overbought RSI, an upper-band close and below-average volume argue for waiting for broader confirmation of the recovery. Costco has a relatively resilient consumption profile under the verified spending backdrop. Cost pressure and the rate increase offset that support, leaving the macro layer neutral. The bear carries the current-price objection because comparable-demand quality does not demonstrate owner-cash value at 44.49x vendor earnings. Annual growth survives tariff normalisation, so a business-decline sell thesis is unsupported. Normalised membership economics and cash valuation are required for a stronger purchase ruling. Strongest counterweight considered: Annual net sales grew 10.1%, earnings increased to $9.226bn from $8.099bn and adjusted comparables rose 6.6%; these establish genuine operating progress independent of the $0.15 quarterly refund.
bull_case: Costco has observed sales, earnings and adjusted comparable-sales growth. Round two preserves comparable-demand strength after excluding the tariff refund and frames the case as durable operations at a justified normalised valuation.
bear_case: The bear accepts demand progress independent of the refund but retains the 44.49x snapshot multiple as an unanswered price hurdle. Debt, FCF and membership economics are unreconciled, and the overbought rebound below SMA-200 does not establish an entry advantage.
key_uncertainties: Debt, FCF and normalised membership economics.
Owner-cash valuation and persistence of comparable growth.
Durable recovery rather than an overbought low-volume rebound.
Persistence of comparable-demand growth and normalised membership economics.
Margin for slower growth at the snapshot premium and durable price recovery.
Vendor financial statements lack verified fiscal/availability timing; vendor forward P/E is an estimate, and a matched normalised fair-value model is unavailable.
catalysts_upcoming: Next comparable issuer disclosure, date unavailable here: A subsequent comparable annual adjusted comparable-sales growth rate at or below zero would invalidate the retained demand-duration premise.

Reassessment trigger rather than a forecast: A matched primary cash/debt and membership-earnings bridge shows positive normalised earnings growth and post-investment/service cash above zero, resolving the central owner-cash gap and requiring entry-value reassessment.
